newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Commerce official John Huang ordered subpoenaed.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Commerce official John Huang ordered subpoenaed.

text.p: A judge Wednesday ordered that a subpoena be served on former Commerce Department official John Huang in a civil case by a conservative legal group not directly related to his fund-raising controversy.

U.S. District Judge Royce Lamberth granted a request by the group, Judicial Watch, which wants to question Huang and others to determine if the Commerce Department used trade missions to improperly raise funds for Democrats.
The judge told the U.S. Marshal to serve the subpoena and asked the Commerce Department to provide to the group the most recent address and telephone number for Huang.

The group sued the Commerce Department nearly two years ago, claiming the agency failed to release documents requested under the freedom-of-information law regarding trade missions led by the late Secretary Ron Brown.
On Friday, the judge allowed the group to question Huang and another former department official, Melinda Yee.

From the Commerce Department, Huang became vice-chairman of the Democratic National Committee's finance arm. He was removed from his fund-raising duties last week after questions were raised about contributions he helped solicit.

The judge also said Judicial Watch may subpoena Brown's wife, Alma, for his Commerce Department files alleged to be in public storage. He also said it may subpoena former Commerce Department special counsel Ira Sockowitz about any files in his possession.
